intro: Surgical technologists monitor procedures, prepare equipment and anticipate surgeons' needs, skills that therapy and imaging careers share. The closest of the 25 careers below are Surgical Assistants and Radiation Therapists, both at an 82% match; radiation therapists earn a BLS May 2025 median of $105,310, or 63% more than the $64,650 surgical technologists earn.
why_it_works: In the operating room you keep instruments sterile, track every item and stay a step ahead of the surgeon. O*NET rates operations monitoring at 3.25 out of 5 for this job, and service orientation and time management at 3.12. Radiation therapy, respiratory care and endoscopy use the same precision. Almost every match needs no new degree, though most need a certification.
tips: Radiation therapy is the strongest move: same preparation level, much higher pay.
Respiratory Therapists earn $82,280, which is 27% more, after an associate program.
Nurse Anesthetists earn $236,590 but need nursing school and a graduate degree.

faq.q: What jobs can former surgical technologists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Surgical Assistants (82%), Radiation Therapists (82%) and Respiratory Therapists (77%), based on O*NET 31.0. Surgical Assistants earn $66,800, which is 3% more than the $64,650 surgical technologist median, and take on more hands-on tasks during surgery.

faq.q: Which careers for surgical technologists pay more?
faq.a: 10 of the 25 matches pay more. Nurse Anesthetists earn $236,590 (266% more), Nuclear Technicians $110,240 (71% more) and Radiation Therapists $105,310 (63% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nurse anesthesia usually needs nursing school plus a graduate degree.

faq.q: Do surgical technologists need more education to switch?
faq.a: Usually not a new degree. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than surgical technologists already have, including all of the top 10. An associate degree is common, held by 50% of workers in a close match, though each field has its own certification exam.

faq.q: What skills should surgical technologists learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are programming, social perceptiveness, operations analysis and systems analysis. Coordination already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so learning to run treatment or imaging equipment is the main step for most moves.
